title: Power Apps: display density settings for model-driven apps
summary: Hold: the statement that Learn documents no way to force a density overlooks the documented Off setting, which forces Comfortable and ignores users' stored preferences. The roadmap facts, licensing background and automation are supported; the app-setting route also needs a small clarification.

claims.claim: Users reach density through the app header Settings menu > Personal settings > Appearance > Display density.
claims.quote:
In a model-driven app, open the Settings menu on the app header.
Select Personal settings.
Select the Appearance tab.
Under Display density, select one of the following options:

claims.claim: Power Apps (maker) > Solutions > solution > Display density > Edit setting value > Setting environment value > New value reaches the environment override.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Solutions.
Select the setting definition.
In the Edit setting value dialog, in the Setting environment value section, select New value.

claims.claim: The solution steps require Solution preview on, enabled by selecting Solution preview off when displayed.
claims.quote: From the Solutions area in Power Apps, on the command bar, ensure you have Solution preview on. If Solution preview off is displayed, select the option to enable the preview.

claims.claim: An existing Display density setting can first be added to a solution through Add existing > More > Setting.
claims.quote:
In the command bar, select Add existing > More > Setting.
In the Add existing setting definition dialog, select one or more settings that you want to add.

claims.claim: POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue creates or updates the environment override using SettingName and Value, without AppUniqueName.
claims.quote:
Creates or updates app/organization level override.
AppUniqueName: Model-driven app unique name (Optional).
SettingName: Setting definition unique name (Required).
Value: Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: Power Apps (maker) > Solutions > solution > app > Edit > Settings reaches the dialog holding the app density setting.
claims.quote:
In the app designer select Settings on the command bar.
When you select Settings from the command bar, select Features to enable or disable model-driven app features for the app.
claims.fix: Keep the route, which correctly reaches Settings. Add to its note: 'In Settings, Features displays generally available settings and Upcoming displays preview settings; select the applicable tab and edit Display density.' This is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/create-edit-configure-settings#setting-app-value.

claims.quote: Searched: "display density" force enforce administrator permissions roles. Read appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings. The appearance page names admins and makers, but specifies no exact security role or privilege.

claims.quote: Searched: "display density" "SettingName" unique name SaveSettingValue. Read appearance-settings and SaveSettingValue; reviewed get-update-setting-value-using-code search excerpt. The appearance page names no density-specific API.

claims.claim: The Display density setting definition's unique name is not published in the referenced pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "display density" "SettingName" unique name SaveSettingValue. Read appearance-settings, create-edit-configure-settings and SaveSettingValue. UserSettings names the personal displaydensity column, not the app setting definition's unique name.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe a way to force a density on users who have not chosen Auto.
claims.quote:
When display density is off:
The app uses Comfortable density.
The display density options are hidden from users.
Any stored display density preference for the user is ignored.
claims.fix: Remove 'Learn does not describe a way to force a density on users who have not chosen Auto.' The preceding sentence already gives the correct Off exception; the documented Off setting forces Comfortable even when a user has a different stored preference.

claims.claim: The general settings mechanism has a definition default, an optional environment override and an optional app override that takes precedence.
claims.quote:
Setting app value is used to override the setting's default value and any setting environment value for a single app.
If a setting environment value does not exist, use a setting app value when the setting's default value is not what you want

claims.claim: Makers enable the header refresh through Solutions > solution > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote:
In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar.
Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.
